questions.q: When $999999\dots$ ($104$ times) is divided by $271$, the remainder that remains is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Repdigit Cyclicity)

Dekh bhai, prime numbers ki repeating digits me cyclic property (magic multiples) hoti hai. $271$ ka relation $9$ series me kahan banta hai, ye pata hona chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Tujhe pata hona chahiye $271 \times 369 = 99999$ (5 baar 9). Matlab har $5$ baar $9$ ka block $271$ se completely divide hoke $0$ remainder dega.
Total digits hain $104$. Isko $5$ ke blocks me tod do: $104 \div 5$, bacha $4$ digits.
Pehle $100$ digits consume ho gaye. End me sirf $4$ digits bache: $9999$.
Ab bs $9999 \div 271$ karna hai. $271 \times 36 = 9756$.
$9999 - 9756 = 243$. Answer aa gaya!

Future Exam Takeaway: Magic numbers yaad kar le: $1001 = 7 \times 11 \times 13$, aur $99999 = 271 \times 369 \times 1$. Cyclicity ka length digit grouping me kaam aata hai.

questions.q: What will be the unit digit of $(137^{13})^{47}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Exponents multiplied honge. $(a^m)^n = a^{m \times n}$. Seedha unit digit of base aur combined power par focus karna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $137^{13 \times 47} = 137^{611}$.
Ab power 611 ko 4 se bhag dena hai. 4 ke divisibility rule se sirf last 2 digits 11 ko divide kar. Remainder aayega 3.
Base ka unit digit 7 hai, toh naya expression bacha $7^3 = 343$. Last digit 3. Tick maar aur aage nikal!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Bracket ka dhyan rakhna. $(a^m)^n = a^{mn}$ hota hai, lekin $a^{m^n}$ me power alag banti hai. SSC hamesha bracket lagake deta hai to simplify.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Kitni bhi lambi powers multiply me hon, sabka alag alag modulo 4 nikal ke final mod nikal sakte ho (Remainder theorem in powers).

questions.q: Evaluate: $2.\overline{75} + 3.\overline{78}$
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, $2+3=5$ hoga aur $75+78 > 100$ hoga, yani ek 1 idhar aayega carry over hoke, toh answer 6 point something banega. Fractional conversion mat karne lag jana.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Chup-chaap expand karke vertically add kar de:
$\phantom{+}2.757575$
$+3.787878$
------------
$\phantom{+}6.545453$
Kyunki series aage continuous hai, agle step se bhi ek 1 carry aayega, toh ye exact $6.545454\dots$ ban jayega.
Result = $6.\overline{54}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
$\frac{75}{99} + \frac{78}{99} = \frac{153}{99} = 1 \frac{54}{99}$.
Toh $2 + 3 + 1\frac{54}{99} = 6 + \frac{54}{99} = 6.\overline{54}$.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Bar addition/subtraction mein humesha numbers ko 3-4 baar likh kar vertical add karna is the safest hack.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $1^{2^3} \times 2^{3^4} \times 3^{4^5} \times \dots \times 9^{10^{11}}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Pure expression mein series ki range dekh. Is series mein 5 aur Even numbers ka product ho raha hai. Jab bhi 5 aur koi Even number milte hain, toh tail digit me zero aana lazmi hai!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Ek term aayega $5^{6^7}$. 5 ki koi bhi power ho, aakhiri digit hamesha 5 rehti hai. Doosra term aayega $2^{3^4}$, jo ek Even number hai. Rule yaad rakh bhai: $5 \times \text{Even} = 0$. Unit place pe hamesha ZERO (0) aayega. Calculation karna hi bewakoofi hai isme!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Unit digit of $x^n$ mostly cyclicity pe nirbhar karta hai. Par jab series me multiplication ho, toh sabse pehle zeroes check karte hain. 5 aur kisi bhi multiple of 2 ke combine hone par 10 banta hai, trailing digit fixed to 0.

Future Exam Takeaway: Multiplication series dekhte hi $5$ aur Even numbers ko scan karo (Unit Digit Method OP).

questions.q: Four bells ring simultaneously at starting and an interval of 6 sec, 12 sec, 15 sec and 20 sec respectively. How many times they ring together in 2 hours?
questions.s:
Answer is 121.

Pen-Free Observation: Bhai isme exam setter bachcho ko hamesha '+1' wale trap me fansata hai. 'Simultaneously at starting' bola hai, matlab 0th second wala bhi count hoga.

Method 1 (Exam Approach):
LCM of intervals (6, 12, 15, 20) = 60 seconds (1 minute).
Matlab har 1 minute baad sab ek saath bajeingi.
Total time = 2 hours = 120 minutes.
Number of intervals = $\frac{120}{1} = 120$.
Total times they ring together = $120 + 1 \text{ (starting wali)} = 121$.

Answer is 2.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, power ki bhi power hai! Ghabrana nahi hai. Unit digit hamesha base ke aakhri digit aur power ki cyclicity (4) par depend karta hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
1st term $37^{38^{39}}$: Base 7 hai. Power $38^{39}$ ek even number hai. Agar 38 ko 4 se divide karein toh remainder 2 aayega. Toh $(4k+2)^{\text{odd}} \implies$ hamesha 4 ka multiple hoga. Matlab power perfectly divisible by 4. $7^4$ ka unit digit hamesha 1 hota hai.
2nd term $39^{38^{37}}$: Base 9 hai. Power $38^{37}$ even number hai. 9 ki power even ho toh unit digit hamesha 1 aata hai.
Total sum: $1 + 1 = 2$.

Takeaway: SSC CGL Mains me aese hi darate hain, bas cyclicity ka rule yaad rakhna!

questions.q: If $732XY$ is a number which is divisible by 70, then find minimum value of $(X+Y)/2$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Base Isolation)

Dekh bhai... composite rules ko humesha unit digit set karne ke liye pehle kaatna chahiye.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 70 se divisible hai toh 10 se bhi hoga, matlab aakhiri digit $Y$ strictly 0 ho gaya.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
Ab bacha 7. $732X$ ko 7 se divide karna hai.
$7320 \pmod 7 = 5$. Toh $(5 + X)$ ko 7 se divisible banana hai.
Minimum $X$ aayega 2.
Value maangi hai $\frac{X+Y}{2}$ ki, toh $\frac{2+0}{2} = 1$. Option elimination aur digital hacks ka sahi prayog kar.

Future Exam Takeaway: Always satisfy the 10, 5, or 2 divisibility rule first to lock the unit digit, then solve for the remaining primes.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which is perfectly divisible by $7$, but when divided by $6, 9,$ and $15$ leaves a remainder of $4$ in each case.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Number $7$ se divisible hona chahiye. Options check karo! $94, 184, 544$ $7$ se nahi katte. Sirf $364$ kat raha hai. Exam me solve karna hi nahi tha!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Maths approach: $\text{LCM}$ of $6, 9, 15 = 90$.
Number is of the form $90k + 4$.
Condition: $(90k + 4)$ is divisible by $7$.
Find remainder of $90/7 \implies 6$. So, $(6k + 4)$ must be div by $7$.
Put $k=4 \implies 6(4)+4 = 28$ (divisible by $7$).
Original Number $= 90(4) + 4 = 364$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
We reduce $90k \pmod 7$ to make calculation smaller. $90 = 12 \times 7 + 6$. Hamesha remainder equation bana ke minimum $k$ dhoondo.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Aise sawalo me sabse pehle divisibility rule lagao options par. $90\%$ cases me $1$ hi option match karega aur $5$ seconds me mark karke aage badh jaoge!

questions.q: Find the last two digits of the sequence $1234\dots$ up to exactly $138$ digits.
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Unitary Scaling.

Pen-Free Observation: Dekh bhai, counting series ka boundary wala khel hai. $1$ se $9$ tak $9$ digits ud gaye, baaki saare 2-digit number sequence banayenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): Bache hue digits ko 2 se divide kar. Kitne pure numbers aaye aur kitna remainder bacha (jo aakhiri kata hua digit hoga) wo nikal le.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Remaining Digits} = 138 - 9 = 129 \\ \frac{129}{2} = 64 \text{ full numbers } + 1 \text{ extra digit} \\ \text{Last full number} = 9 + 64 = 73 \\ \text{Next number starts with } 7 \text{ (from } 74) \\ \text{Sequence ends:} \dots 72, 73, 7 \implies \text{Last two} = 37 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Series logic se hume exactly nikalna padta hai ki counting kahan tak pahuchegi. Arithmetic counting formula check karo.

Mathematically :-

$$ d(1 \dots N) = 9 + 2(N - 9) \text{ for 2-digit } N \\ 9 + 2(N - 9) = 137 \text{ (closest even match)} \\ 2(N - 9) = 128 \implies N = 73 \\ 138\text{th digit is first digit of } 74, \text{ which is } 7 $$

TCS Trap: Options me seedha $74$ baithega taki tum '1 extra digit' bhool kar pura 74 append karke tick mar do.

Exam Takeaway:

> Hamesha block break karo. $1-9$ = 9 digits. $10-99$ = 180 digits. Extra digit hamesha next number ki starting place nikalta hai.

questions.q: If the 8-digit number $8439x53y$ is divisible by $99$, then what is the value of $(x^2 + y^2)$?
questions.s:
Final Output: $16$

Core Conceptual Tool: Divisibility & C9.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisibility $99$ matlab co-primes $11$ aur $9$. Do variables ke liye do linear equations ban ke unko side-by-side solve karna padega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): 11 ke alternate sum ko aur 9 ke regular sum ko barabar le aao ek system me.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{For } 11: (y+5+9+4) - (3+x+3+8) = 18+y - 14-x = 4+y-x \implies x-y=4 \\ \text{For } 9: 32+x+y \pmod 9 = 0 \implies x+y=4 \\ x=4, y=0 \implies 4^2 + 0^2 = 16 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ye linear systems over digits hain. Check limits, variables must strictly be between $0$ and $9$.

Mathematically :-

$$ x - y = 4 \\ x + y = 4 \text{ or } 13 \\ \text{Solving gives } x=4, y=0 \text{ (Valid digit constraint)} $$

TCS Trap: TCS me tum variables solve karte hue sum 13 le loge equation me, jisse answer point/fraction ban jayega aur time kill hoga.

Exam Takeaway:

> Variables set karte time simultaneously rule of 9 aur 11 ko check karo ki single digits $0-9$ ke bounds break na ho jayein.

questions.q: $846523X7Y$ is a 9 digit number which is divisible by $9$, and $Y-X=6$. Find the value of $\sqrt{2X+4Y}$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Digital Root Balancing)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... C9 method lagana hai, poora joddna time waste hai.

Pen-Free Observation: $9$ ka rule matlab Digital Sum $9$ hona chahiye. Sum nikalte waqt $9$ banne wale pairs wahin uda do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Remaining digits ka sum: $8+6+2+3+7 = 26 \implies 8$. Matalab $8 + X + Y$ ko $9$ se katna hai. Yani $X+Y$ ki value ya toh $1$ hogi ya $10$.
Given: $Y - X = 6$. Agar $X+Y=1$ liya toh values negative aayengi.
Toh $X+Y = 10$ aur $-X+Y = 6$ solve kar. Jodd de: $2Y = 16 \implies Y=8$. Toh $X=2$.
Equation me daal: $\sqrt{2(2) + 4(8)} = \sqrt{4 + 32} = \sqrt{36} = 6$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): C9 method me sum chota karke simultaneous equation me ghusa do.

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisibility of $9$ dekhte hi sab digits joddne nahi baithna, $9$ ke multiples ko raaste me hi cancel karte jao.

questions.q: If the 6-digit number $213x4y$ is divisible by 99, find the value of $(x + y)$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Balancing)

Dekh bhai... 99 matlab 11 aur 9 dono se divisible hona chahiye. Aise case mein 11 ki condition hamesha linear equation deti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: 11 ka rule alternate digit sum hota hai, jo humein variables mein direct relation dega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique):
11 ka rule laga: Alternate sum $(2+3+4) - (1+x+y) = 9 - (1+x+y) = 8 - (x+y)$.
Yeh 11 se divisible tabhi hoga jab yeh 0 bane, kyunki $x, y$ digits hain aur inka max sum 18 ho sakta hai (so -3 possible nahi). So $x+y = 8$.
Cross check with 9: Sum of digits = $10+x+y = 18$, jo 9 se divisible hai. Done!

Future Exam Takeaway: For composite divisors like 99, 88, 72, always hit the 11 or 8 divisibility rule first. It locks the variables instantly.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $53^{105}$ is divided by 17?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisor 17 ek prime number hai. Ye clear hint hai Fermat's Little Theorem lagane ka.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Pehle base reduce karo: $53 \div 17 \rightarrow$ Remainder 2 (kyunki $17 \times 3 = 51$).
New expression: $2^{105} \pmod{17}$.
Fermat theorem kehti hai $A^{P-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{P}$. Yani power cycle 16 ki chalegi.
105 ko 16 se divide kar power choti karne ke liye: $105 = 16 \times 6 + 9$.
Remainder power bachi 9.
Expression bana: $2^9 \pmod{17}$.
$2^9 = 512$. Ab 512 ko 17 se bhag kar do.
$17 \times 30 = 510$. Remainder seedha 2 bacha!

Future Exam Takeaway:
Bade base wale numbers pehle reduce karo division karke, phir power ko Euler ya Fermat theorem se udhao.

questions.q: Determine the unit digit of $98^{99^{100^{101}}}$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Base $8$ hai, toh cyclicity $4$ ki lagegi. Power dekh ke ghabrana nahi, sirf parity (odd/even) ka game hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Power ko $4$ se divide karo: $99 \pmod 4 = 3 \equiv -1$.
Ab is $99$ ke upar ki power dekho: $100^{101}$, jo ki definitely ek EVEN number hai.
$(-1)^{\text{Even}} = +1$. Matlab reduced effective power $1$ ho gayi.
Unit digit = $8^1 = 8$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Power of power (ladder exponent) me humesha base of ladder ko mod cyclicity karte hain. Phir uske exponent ka nature (odd ya even) check karte hain.

Future Exam Takeaway:
CDS aur SSC aise hi power ladders dete hain time waste karne ke liye. Modulo $4$ aur Odd/Even nature se ye $5$ second me break hota hai.

questions.q: The square of any prime number greater than 3, when divided by 24, always leaves a remainder of:
questions.s:
Answer is 1.

Pen-Free Observation: 3 se bada koi bhi prime number assume karle, jaise 5 ya 7. Square kar aur 24 se divide kar. $25/24$ rem 1, $49/24$ rem 1. Khel khatam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Koi bhi prime number $>3$ humesha $6k \pm 1$ ki form mein hota hai.
Square it: $(6k \pm 1)^2 = 36k^2 \pm 12k + 1 = 12k(3k \pm 1) + 1$.
Ab dekh bhai, $k(3k \pm 1)$ hamesha even hoga (put $k=1,2,3...$). Matlab yeh poori term $12 \times \text{even} = 24m$ ban jayegi.
So, $24m + 1$ ko 24 se divide karega toh Remainder strictly 1 aayega.

questions.q: If the number $555\dots$ (repeated 100 times) is divided by 37, what is the remainder?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Dekh bhai, 37 ka magic number dekhte hi dimag mein 3-digit repeating blocks (111, 222, 555) chamakne chahiye. 100 ko 3 se divide karega toh 1 remainder bachega, yani aakhiri ka 1 digit hi answer decide karega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Har 3 digit ka set (555) 37 se poori tarah cancel ho jayega.
100 digits = 33 blocks of 3 digits + 1 extra digit.
99 digits tak remainder 0 ho gaya. Bacha sirf aakhiri digit, jo ki 5 hai. Wahi tera remainder hai.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Rule of 37: $37 \times 3 = 111$. Isliye koi bhi digit agar 3 baar repeat ho, wo 111 ka multiple ban jata hai aur automatically 37 se divide hota hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Agar question mein $999\dots$ (101 times) de de, toh $101 \div 3 \rightarrow$ Remainder 2. Yani last ke do digit (99) ko 37 se bhag de dena.

questions.q: If $68A3Y$ is divisible by $3, 7$ and $11$, find $4A+3Y$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Divisibility by $3, 7$, and $11$ means divisible by their LCM, $3 \times 7 \times 11 = 231$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Assume max possible value $68939$ and divide by $231$.
$68939 \div 231 = 298$ (Quotient) and Remainder = $101$.
Subtract remainder to get perfect multiple: $68939 - 101 = 68838$.
Compare $68838$ with $68A3Y \implies A = 8, Y = 8$.
Value of $4A + 3Y = 4(8) + 3(8) = 32 + 24 = 56$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Alternating sums for $11$ and digital roots for $3$ can also form equations, but LCM subtraction is fool-proof and fastest.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Whenever a number with missing digits is divisible by $7, 11, 13$ or $3, 7, 11$, always pad it with $9$s, find the remainder with LCM, and subtract!

questions.q: If all the factors of 800 are written in ascending order, find out which factor will occupy the 15th position.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Bhai factors hamesha pairs me aate hain ($1 \times 800, 2 \times 400$). Peeche se position check karna easy padega kyunki ascending me 15th matlab total me se peeche ki taraf aana.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Pehle 800 ke total factors nikal le: $800 = 2^5 \times 5^2$.
Total factors = $(5+1)(2+1) = 6 \times 3 = 18$.
Humein 15th factor pucha hai. Matlab peeche se 4th factor! ($18, 17, 16, 15$).
Largest factors divide karne se milte hain: $1 \rightarrow 800$ (18th), $2 \rightarrow 400$ (17th), $4 \rightarrow 200$ (16th), $5 \rightarrow 160$ (15th).
Yani 15th position pe 160 baitha hai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Factor pairs ka rule kehta hai $a \times b = N$. Jahaan $a$ badhega, $b$ chhota hoga. $N$ ko initial natural numbers se divide karte raho, last terms descending me sequence me mil jayenge.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi higher position factor pooche, total nikal kar peeche se reverse order chalao.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $232^{123^{321}}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Unit digit nikalni hai, base ka last digit $2$ hai. Yani cyclicity $4$ check hogi. Power of power ladder me trick lagao.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Power hai $123^{321}$. Ise $4$ se mod karo.
$123 \pmod 4 \equiv 3 \equiv -1$.
Reduced effective power $= (-1)^{321}$. Since power is Odd, it stays $-1$.
Math me $-1$ mod $4$ ka actual remainder hota hai: $4 - 1 = 3$.
Base unit $2^3 = 8$. Bam!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Negative remainders cyclicity calculations ke Brahmastra hote hain. Jab base cyclicity-divisor ke close ho (jaise $123 = 124 - 1$), $-1$ assume karne se power odd-even logic se ek second me tut jati hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
For any $X^{Y^Z}$ unit digit question, immediately apply modulo $4$ on base $X$'s power ladder using $+1$ or $-1$ deviation.

questions.q: $x, y,$ and $z$ are distinct prime numbers where $x < y < z$. If $x + y + z = 70$, then what is the maximum possible value of $z$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Parity Property)

Dekh bhai, ye basic properties pe khelne wala question hai. Numbers ko dekh ke dar mat.

Pen-Free Observation: Teen prime numbers ka sum $70$ (Even) hai. Teen odd numbers ka sum kabhi even nahi ho sakta. Matalab ek prime lazmi taur par $2$ hoga!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Sabse chota prime $x = 2$ set kar diya. Bacha $y + z = 68$. $z$ ko maximum karna hai toh options se check kar. Agar $z = 67$ (prime), toh $y = 1$ (not prime, reject). Agar $z = 61$ (prime), toh $y = 7$ (prime, accept!). Done.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Prime number set me sirf $2$ hi ek akela even warrior hai. Ye SSC/CDS ka favourite trap hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi 3 prime numbers ka sum Even diya ho, toh aankh band karke sabse chote number ko $2$ maan lena.

questions.q: How many zeroes are there in the product $4^6 \times 15^{10}$?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Zeroes ki factory me sirf do hi worker hote hain: 2 aur 5. Jab tak dono milke ek pair nahi banate, zero nahi banta. Powers check kar jiska number kam hoga, utne zeroes honge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Base numbers ko unke prime form (2 aur 5) me tod.
$4^6 = (2^2)^6 = 2^{12}$. (Worker '2' ki quantity = 12).
$15^{10} = (3 \times 5)^{10} = 3^{10} \times 5^{10}$. (Worker '5' ki quantity = 10).
Jode (pairs) wahi tak banenge jitne kam worker honge. Yahan minimum quantity 10 hai (5 walon ki). Toh seedha answer 10 zero milenge end mein!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Number of trailing zeroes is entirely defined by $\min(x, y)$ in the prime factorization $2^x \times 5^y$. The extra 3s from $3^{10}$ are irrelevant to trailing zeroes.

Future Exam Takeaway: Composite bases dekhte hi sabse pehle 2 aur 5 me expand karo aur minimum power pick karlo.

questions.q: What will be the quotient when $x$ is divided by 462, where $x$ is the smallest 6-digit number that leaves a remainder of 5 when divided by 20, 21, 22, 24, and 28?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Equation me $x$ pucha hi nahi hai, Quotient pucha hai 462 se divide karne pe. Reverse engineering aur options approximation ka behtareen combo lagao!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Bhai $x$ ki value $462 \times Q + R$ hogi. Yahan Quotient options 220 ke aas paas hain. $462 \times 220 = 101640$.
Agar isme remainder 5 jodenge toh 101645 aayega.
Kya yeh 101640 number 20, 21, 22, 24, 28 se divide hota hai? Haan, kyunki piche zero hai (20 se cut gaya), aur 21 (multiples of 3 aur 7), 22 (11 ka multiple) se easily divisible lag raha hai. Seedha Option B confirm, bina LCM banaye solve ho gaya!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Proper tarike me LCM(20, 21, 22, 24, 28) nikalna padega jo 9240 aayega. Smallest 6-digit multiple nikalne ke liye 100000/9240 karo $\approx 10.8$, so upper multiple $11 \times 9240 = 101640$. Usme 5 jodo toh $x=101645$ aaya. Ab use 462 se divide karoge toh 220 baar me jayega.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab options me result quotient form me ho, to base multiply marke range cross check karna sabse fast hack hota hai. Step 1: Observation of Numbers Tujhe pata hai number ki format kya hogi: x = \text{LCM} \times k + 5. Divisor kya diya hai question me? 462. Zra LCM ke numbers (20, 21, 22, 24, 28) ko dhyan se dekh. Kya 462 inme chupa hai? Haan! 21 \times 22 = 462. Step 2: Relation Between LCM and Divisor Tujhe pura LCM (9240) nikalne ki zaroorat nahi thi. Tujhe bas ye dekhna hai ki LCM 462 ka kitna guna hai. LCM of (20, 21, 22, 24, 28) nikalte waqt: 462 toh aayega hi (kyunki 21 aur 22 base numbers hain). Bacha kya? 20 (yahan se 10 aayega), etc. Actual LCM = 9240. Notice kar: 9240 = 462 \times 20. Step 3: The Killer Move Toh hamari original equation x = \text{LCM} \times k + 5 ban gayi: x = (462 \times 20) \times k + 5 x = 462 \times (20k) + 5 Agar tu is number ko 462 se divide karega, toh Quotient hamesha kya aayega? Quotient = 20k Iska seedha sa matlab hai: Answer (Quotient) HAMESHA 20 ka multiple hoga! (Matlab uske end me minimum ek '0' hona mandatory hai). Step 4: Check Options A) 224 B) 220 ✅ (Only multiple of 20) C) 221 D) 226

questions.q: Determine the last two digits of $35^{42}$.
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First: Number $5$ pe end ho raha hai, toh base ka tens digit aur power ka nature hi result decide karega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, Aman Sir ka fix rule hai:
List I (Tens Digit of Base & Power)List II (Last Two Digits)
A. Both are ODD1. $75$
B. Any other combination2. $25$

Yahan $35^{42}$ mein Tens digit $3$ (Odd) hai, aur Power $42$ (Even) hai. 'Both Odd' wali condition fail ho gayi, toh bina calculation kare seedha $25$ tick maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Cyclicity of $5$ shows that powers of numbers ending in $5$ follow a strict modulo $100$ cycle depending solely on the parity of the preceding digit and the exponent. It's essentially $(10x+5)^{2k}$.

Future Exam Takeaway: CGL me $5$ ending values ki last two digits ke lie ye shortcut hamesha $2$ sec me answer dega.

questions.q: The total number of integers between $200$ and $400$, each of which either begins with $3$ or ends with $3$ or both, is
questions.s:
Core Conceptual Tool: Option Elimination.

Pen-Free Observation: Bhai ekdum pichle type ki xerox copy hai sawal. Same frame, same counting base, same answer form.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique): $300$ wali puri line uthao ($100$ numbers). Fir bach gaya $200$ series, usme har 10 digit me ek baar last me $3$ aata hai. Total 10 nikal ke jod.

Mathematically :-

$$ \text{Starts with 3: } 300 \dots 399 \implies 100 \\ \text{Ends with 3 in 200s: } 203, 213 \dots 293 \implies 10 \\ \text{Sum} = 100 + 10 = 110 $$

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Wahi venn diagram lagti hai yaha, 3 start, 3 end and common numbers in 300s series.

Mathematically :-

$$ n(S_3) = 100, n(E_3) = 20 \\ n(S_3 \cap E_3) = 10 \text{ (like 303, 313...)} \\ \text{Total} = 100 + 20 - 10 = 110 $$

TCS Trap: Statement me likha "or both" padh ke log confuse hoke $110$ me phirse intersection wale $10$ add karke $120$ mark marte hain.

Exam Takeaway:

> Union function "or both" ki condition apne formula block $n(A \cup B)$ me automatic handle karta hai, alag se add nahi karte.

questions.q: If $N = 4^{11} + 4^{12} + 4^{13} + 4^{14}$, then how many positive factors of $N$ are there?
questions.s:
The 'Pen-Free' Observation First:
Terms geometric progression me add ho rahi hain. Sabse choti power common lene se ek prime factorization nikal aayegi jisse number of factors milenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Dekh bhai, $4^{11}$ common le: $4^{11} (1 + 4 + 16 + 64) = 4^{11} \times 85$.
Ab isko strict prime bases me tod: $4^{11} = (2^2)^{11} = 2^{22}$. Aur $85 = 5^1 \times 17^1$.
Toh $N = 2^{22} \times 5^1 \times 17^1$.
Number of factors ke liye powers me +1 kar ke multiply: $(22+1)(1+1)(1+1) = 23 \times 2 \times 2 = 92$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder):
Galti log ye karte hain ki base 4 pe hi powers add kar dete hain. Number of factors ke formula $P=(a+1)(b+1)$ me hamesha base ko Prime number hi rakhna padta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway:
Factor patterns ke expression me prime bases ka conversion kabhi skip mat karna varna seedha zero milega.
